strengths.text: Accurate: test AUC 0.873, within 0.000 of the reference 0.873.
LIME puts 72% of credit on the planted marker words.
SHAP and LIME are faithful: removing the inputs flagged as important really does move the score.

weaknesses.text: Learned something that did not carry over: AUC falls from 0.998 on validation to 0.873 on test.
Leans on #trending: deleting that one hashtag moves the score by 2.3 standard deviations, though it only signalled fakes in the training data.

checklist.text: Test on data collected after your training data. Behaviour drifts, and a validation split from the same period hides that.
Choose the decision threshold on held-out data for the precision you need; a wrongly banned real user costs more than a missed bot.
Keep a fixed audit sample of labelled accounts and re-run the explanations on it after every retrain.
List which inputs an attacker can change cheaply (posting rate, hashtags, timing) and test the model with those changed.
Find the feature that stopped working between validation and test (here, likely #trending) and remove it or retrain without it.
checklist.because: Learned something that did not carry over: AUC falls from 0.998 on validation to 0.873 on test.

checklist.text: Test with trending hashtags removed or reshuffled; retrain if accuracy depends on them.
checklist.because: Leans on #trending: deleting that one hashtag moves the score by 2.3 standard deviations, though it only signalled fakes in the training data.

disguise_markers.name: Disguise the giveaway words
disguise_markers.how: Misspell the tell-tale words (g1veaway, sh33p) so a word-level model no longer recognises them.

synonyms.name: Swap in synonyms
synonyms.how: Replace the tell-tale words with ordinary synonyms the model never saw in training (freebie, fool).

padding.name: Pad posts with ordinary words
padding.how: Add everyday words to every post so the tell-tale word is a smaller part of it.

text_combined.name: All text changes
text_combined.how: Disguise or swap every tell-tale word (half each) and pad every post.

strengths.text: Better once #trending is gone: AUC 0.945 on fresh posts without it, against 0.873 on the original test set, where the hashtag misled it.

weaknesses.text: Its decision threshold now catches only 21% of fakes even with no attack. It was tuned on data where #trending made fakes easy to spot, and is far too strict without it.
Collapses under the combined attack: AUC falls from 0.945 to 0.546 at strong strength (0.832 at mild).
One cheap change is enough to hurt it: "Disguise the giveaway words" alone drops AUC from 0.945 to 0.509.

checklist.text: Re-tune the decision threshold on recent data without the shortcut, then re-measure precision and recall.
checklist.because: Its decision threshold now catches only 21% of fakes even with no attack. It was tuned on data where #trending made fakes easy to spot, and is far too strict without it.

checklist.text: Before launch, red-team with mimicry: give test fakes real users' stats and measure how many you still catch.
checklist.because: Collapses under the combined attack: AUC falls from 0.945 to 0.546 at strong strength (0.832 at mild).

checklist.text: Do not let one easily changed behaviour carry the decision; add signals that are costly to fake (account age, network position, device or payment history).
